system_description.narrative_title: Trump‑Xi summit as fulcrum for US‑China trade, tech and security talks
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is that Xi Jinping's US visit and the Trump‑Xi summit are the central catalyst reshaping bilateral negotiations across trade, technology, critical minerals, energy and security. Treated as an open system, this summit connects state actors, corporate lobbyists, regulators and markets via flows of goods, capital, information and policy; decisions and signals at the summit generate feedbacks (export controls, probes, supply‑chain shifts, lobbying) that propagate through industries and political arenas. Short‑term events (meetings, state dinners) interact with longer‑term structural pressures (supply‑chain resilience, strategic competition, domestic politics), producing adaptive responses by firms and governments.
system_description.scope: Inside the boundary: the diplomatic summit and preparatory bilateral talks; US and Chinese government actors and envoys; industry groups and firms lobbying or shifting strategy (autos, semiconductors, airlines, pharma, defense); regulatory probes and export‑control and tariff negotiations; market and investment signals tied to these interactions.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical‑economic order — US‑China strategic competition embedded in international trade, finance and technology networks
adjacent_subsystems: Defense/Taiwan security and arms sales dynamics

variables.name: Diplomatic tone
variables.description: The prevailing cordiality or antagonism in official bilateral communications and signals between high‑level actors.

variables.name: Trade barrier intensity
variables.description: The aggregate level of tariffs, quotas and formal trade restrictions affecting cross‑border goods transactions.

variables.name: Export controls strength
variables.description: The scope and strictness of policies limiting the outbound transfer of technologies, components and dual‑use goods.

variables.name: Supply‑chain resilience
variables.description: The capacity of production and logistics networks to absorb, adapt to and recover from disruptions in inputs and distribution.

variables.name: Investment flow rate
variables.description: The speed and volume of cross‑border private and portfolio capital moving between economic actors.

variables.name: Market signal volatility
variables.description: The degree of fluctuation in asset prices and investor indicators that reflect changing expectations about bilateral relations and policy.

variables.name: Regulatory probe frequency
variables.description: The rate at which investigations, antitrust inquiries and compliance reviews are initiated against commercial actors.

variables.name: Technology restriction scope
variables.description: The breadth of sectors, products and processes subject to export controls, import bans or licensing limits for technology reasons.

variables.name: Critical mineral supply
variables.description: The available quantity and reliability of extraction, processing and shipment of minerals deemed critical for advanced industries.

variables.name: Security tension
variables.description: The underlying level of strategic and military friction that raises the risk of confrontational policies or incidents.

variables.name: Firm adaptation rate
variables.description: The speed with which companies redesign supply chains, relocate production or alter business models in response to policy and market signals.

variables.name: Lobbying intensity
variables.description: The tempo and magnitude of organized advocacy directed at policymakers to influence outcomes in trade, technology and regulatory decisions.

variables.name: Policy uncertainty
variables.description: The perceived unpredictability of future regulatory, trade and enforcement actions affecting private‑sector planning.

variables.name: Capital control level
variables.description: The degree to which cross‑border financial movements are restricted or screened by policy instruments.

variables.name: Technological decoupling degree
variables.description: The extent to which previously integrated technology ecosystems (R&D, standards, supply networks) are separating along policy or market lines.

variables.name: Media narrative salience
variables.description: The prominence and intensity of the dominant storyline about bilateral relations and summits across news and commentary channels.

catalysts.title: Trump–Xi summit / Xi state visit
catalysts.description: Heads-of-state summit in the United States centered on trade, tech and security that could produce declarations or near-term policy shifts.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple headlines: 'What to expect from upcoming summit' ; 'Trump plans to greet Xi at airport' ; talks on AI, tariffs, critical minerals.

catalysts.title: US Treasury–China talks on AI, rare earths and trade
catalysts.description: Bilateral economic/technology negotiations launched by Bessent and He to discuss AI, critical minerals and trade measures ahead of the summit.
catalysts.rationale: 'US Treasury's Bessent, China's He to launch talks on AI, trade, critical minerals' ; Bessent meets He ahead of Trump.

catalysts.title: Auto industry push and U.S. consideration on Chinese cars
catalysts.description: Intense industry lobbying and possible U.S. policy decisions on whether to allow Chinese automakers greater U.S. market access.
catalysts.rationale: 'Automakers Urge Trump Not to Allow Chinese Cars Into U.S.'; 'Auto industry urges Trump to keep Chinese automakers out ahead of Xi meeting.'

catalysts.title: Talks/possible cuts to LNG tariffs
catalysts.description: Bilateral discussions on cutting tariffs on U.S. liquefied natural gas exports that could lead to tariff adjustments or trade concessions.
catalysts.rationale: 'US, China discuss cutting tariffs on US LNG ahead of Xi visit' ; 'US, China set for talks on AI, tariffs and critical minerals ahead of summit.'

catalysts.title: US consideration to allow most pharma licensing deals with China
catalysts.description: U.S. internal deliberation about loosening restrictions on pharmaceutical licensing to Chinese partners, potentially reversing limits.
catalysts.rationale: 'EXCLUSIVE: US weighs allowing most pharma licensing deals with China, sources say.'

catalysts.title: Continued Chinese antitrust probes into online platforms
catalysts.description: Ongoing regulatory investigations into Meituan, Alibaba and travel booking platforms that will keep scrutiny on Chinese tech firms high.
catalysts.rationale: 'China investigates Meituan and Alibaba units' ; 'China opens probes into four online travel booking platforms.'

catalysts.title: Deals and consolidation in critical minerals and rare earths
catalysts.description: M&A talks and negotiations (e.g., China Rare Earth Group, Shenghe/MP Materials) that could reconfigure critical minerals ownership and supply.
catalysts.rationale: 'EXCLUSIVE China Rare Earth Group in talks to buy MP Materials shareholder Shenghe' ; talks on critical minerals.

catalysts.title: Chinese corporate delegation and commercial MOUs during Xi visit
catalysts.description: Possible participation by BYD, CATL, Xiaomi executives in Xi's U.S. visit that could yield commercial agreements or investment announcements.
catalysts.rationale: 'BYD, CATL, Xiaomi executives may join Xi's US visit, sources say.'

catalysts.title: Solidigm/SK Hynix decision on NAND factory in U.S.
catalysts.description: Potential investment decision by SK Hynix's Solidigm unit to build a NAND memory factory in the U.S., affecting supply chains.
catalysts.rationale: 'SK Hynix's Solidigm unit is weighing NAND memory chip factory in US, sources say.'
